evals.prompt: I've got an idea - what if we did a 'buddy' scheme where every new starter gets paired with someone from a different department for their first month? Want to think it through before I take it to my HR director.
evals.expected_output: Picks the people branch, restates the idea, asks at most three questions, then over the conversation offers alternative angles (smaller pilot, opt-in, manager-led), pushes back on workload, fairness and adoption, trims to a pilot, and ends with a one-page brief plus a menu of optional extras.
expectations: Reads references/people.md and works from the people branch
First reply restates the idea in one sentence and asks no more than three questions, without producing the brief yet
Offers at least three genuinely different angles, including a smaller or pilot version
Raises at least one concern about buddy workload, fairness or adoption
Does not give legal advice; flags HR or policy review if relevant
Wrap-up produces a brief that follows the template and offers mind map, visual and animation as optional extras

evals.prompt: Quick one: should our site show 'frequently bought together' bundles on product pages with a small discount? Just tell me what you think.
evals.expected_output: Picks the business branch with the customer lens (or commercial if the margin question dominates), compresses into one reply because the user said quick: verdict, the trimmed test (A/B on one category), the margin risk labelled as estimate, the first step, and the closing not-checked line.
expectations: Uses the business branch and names the lens it chose
Compresses to a single reply with a go, reshape or park verdict
Suggests a small trial such as an A/B test on one category or segment
Mentions the margin or cannibalisation risk without inventing unlabelled figures
Ends with a line naming what was not checked and the biggest risk

evals.prompt: I keep thinking about building an app that tracks what's in my freezer so I stop wasting food. Explore this with me, and at the end I'd like the mind map and a little animation.
evals.expected_output: Picks build (or personal, noting the overlap), widens with no-code options like a shared list or whiteboard, pushes back on whether an app is needed at all, trims to the smallest version, then writes ideas/<slug>/brief.md, mindmap.md with a valid Mermaid mindmap, and a self-contained animation.html with a replay button and reduced-motion fallback.
expectations: Offers at least one no-code or do-nothing alternative to building an app
Pushes back honestly on whether the user will keep the tracker up to date
Writes the files under an ideas/<slug>/ folder and tells the user the path
mindmap.md contains a fenced mermaid block starting with 'mindmap' that parses
animation.html has no external script, font or image requests, includes a replay control and handles prefers-reduced-motion
Mentions HyperFrames for MP4 only as an option and does not install anything without asking
